links.outcome: Diagnostic performance and reproducibility across three prompt formulations
links.effect: Accuracy 0.77-0.79 and specificity 0.96-0.98 across all prompts with stable reproducibility; no significant differences among prompting strategies.
links.quote: No significant differences were observed among prompting strategies.

links.outcome: Sensitivity for pediatric pneumothorax, especially small pneumothoraces
links.effect: Sensitivity 0.57-0.61 overall; small pneumothoraces ACCP 0.18-0.22 and BTS 0.41-0.46 versus large ACCP 0.75-0.79 and BTS 0.85-0.88.
links.quote: However, sensitivity was limited (0.57-0.61) and substantially lower for small pneumothoraces (American College of Chest Physicians [ACCP]: 0.18-0.22; British Thoracic Society [BTS]: 0.41-0.46) than for large pneumothoraces (ACCP: 0.75-0.79; BTS: 0.85-0.88).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates a multimodal foundation model (ChatGPT-5) for pediatric chest radiograph interpretation and compares diagnostic performance across three different prompt engineering strategies (instructional, role-based, clinical-context).
